content.title: About
content.content: Salisbury steak dinner is a ready‑to‑heat frozen meal that includes a seasoned ground‑beef patty prepared in the classic Salisbury style, served with a savory gravy and a side (usually mashed potatoes or vegetables). It belongs to the NFS (National Food Service) line and is designed for quick microwave or stovetop reheating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Salisbury steak was created in the late 19th century by Dr. J. H. Salisbury as a more affordable alternative to a beef filet.
NFS frozen meals are widely used in cafeterias, hotels, and military bases because of their long shelf life.
Each serving provides roughly 350 kcal, making it a convenient balanced‑meal option.
The gravy typically combines beef broth, tomato paste, and spices, giving the dish its distinctive flavor.
The product is sealed in a moisture‑vapor barrier pouch, allowing storage in the freezer for up to 24 months.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: The beef patty supplies about 20 g of high‑quality protein, essential for muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The meal provides vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Vegetable side adds fiber
items.content: The accompanying vegetables contribute dietary fiber, vitamin C, and antioxidants.

items.title: Convenient and quick
items.content: Preparation takes only 3–5 minutes, helping to save time and reduce cooking stress.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: A single serving can contain up to 800 mg of sodium, which should be considered by those monitoring blood pressure.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The gravy may contain wheat flour, making the product unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Need for thorough heating
items.content: Insufficient reheating may leave live bacteria; follow the recommended time and temperature guidelines.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Preservatives are used to extend shelf life, which some consumers may wish to avoid.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the frozen meal directly from the freezer: microwave on high for 3–5 minutes, stirring halfway through to ensure even heating. For a fresher touch, add chopped fresh herbs or a squeeze of lemon before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the meal frozen at –18 °C or lower. Once the package is opened, consume within 24 hours and store the remaining portion in the refrigerator at +4 °C. Do not refreeze.
